hulk cotati.name: Hulk (Cotati)
hulk cotati.species: Cotati inhabiting the body of She-Hulk
hulk cotati.origin: While preparing for their invasion of Earth, the Cotati called the Avengers for help, pretending they were at risk of being wiped out by the Kree/Skrull Alliance. When they arrived on the Blue Area of the Moon, the Swordsman convinced She-Hulk to come with him, stating that she would need a weapon to fight in the oncoming war. The Cotati, however, were lying, and bound her using Centaurian ironwood before killing her and planting a Cotati inside her body in order to infiltrate the Avengers. The Cotati pretended to fight alongside the Avengers and the Fantastic Four as the She-Hulk, and learned that the Kree/Skull alliance planned to detonate the Pyre in order to wipe out the Cotati, even being rid of all life in the Solar System. When Mantis, Susan Storm, and Ben Grimm went to Lake Victoria to convince Quoi to abandon his genocidal war, the Cotati Hulk accompanied them. There it informed Quoi of the Pyre and revealed its ruse before attacking Ben Grimm. The Cotati Hulk repeatedly focused on pummelling Ben rather than fighting Susan or Mantis, who weren't as powerful. Finding no other way to stop them, Susan had Mantis block all pain and fatigue signals from reaching her mind while she held the Cotati Hulk in her force field, in order to allow Ben to convince the real Jennifer to fight the Cotati inhabiting her body. Jen was able to come back to life with the help of the Leader, and fought against the Cotati controlling her after hearing Ben's words, purging them from her body completely.

hulkbot 3000.name: Hulkbot 3000
hulkbot 3000.origin: The Hulkbot 3000 was built by the Smiths, a group of assistant robots that were in turn created by Tony Stark. Intended to imitate the Hulk, the Hulkbot's purpose was to test out a prototype device in the shape of a crown that could modify a person's behavior. Stark claimed the device would be used on Hulk's alter-ego, Bruce Banner, but he was actually looking for a way to find a cure to his alcoholism. thumb|left|The Hulkbot's original angry "face" When Stark and Jim Rhodes were overseeing the Hulkbot, it activated on its own and went on a rampage. Stark put an end on it, using an Iron Man Gauntlet to shoot the Hulkbot's head off. The droid was later repaired and deployed with the intention to battle the Asgardian dragon Sadurang. During battle, Sadurang infected Stark's Iron Man Armor with magic, causing it to transmute. After attemping to fight the dragon despite his lack of skill with magic, Iron Man decided to have the Hulkbot rip its chestplate off, allowing him to remove the suit and change into the Iron Man Armor Model 1.

human torch android.origin: ===Origin=== left|thumb|Professor Phineas T. Horton unveils his creation, the original Human Torch, to an audience of reporters in 1939. The original Human Torch began his existence in 1939 in the laboratory of Professor Phineas T. Horton, one of the pioneers in the field of artificial intelligence and robotics. The culmination of Horton's research was an android who mimicked virtually all of the functions of a human being, including independent thought, but was composed entirely of synthetic materials. Horton worked closely with fellow scientist James Bradley who grew disgusted by Horton's hope for fame and fortune and dissolved their partnership. The one apparent flaw in the android's design concerned the photoelectric solar cells, or "Horton Cells" which covered every square inch of his body and served as his power source. The cells were too volatile and caused the epidermis of the android to burst into flame upon contact with air but without harming the android itself. Horton revealed the Torch's existence to the public at a press conference in November 1939, at which he demonstrated how the Torch would burst into flame if he introduced a small amount of oxygen into the transparent container in which he was confined. The news media proclaimed the Torch to be a potential menace, and so after a meeting with the Scientists Guild and a presidential order, Horton buried the android in his supposedly airtight tube within cement until such time as he could find a way either to prevent the android from bursting into flame or learn how to control its flame. thumb|Accidentally let loose before he could control his powers, the Human Torch created a panic. There was a slow leak in the tube, however, and eventually enough oxygen entered so that the android's flame ignited explosively, permitting him to escape. Wreaking havoc in innocent exploration of his environment, the android, inaccurately dubbed the Human Torch, soon realized the panic he was causing and, unable to control his flaming power, doused his flame in a swimming pool. In his infancy, the Human Torch was duped by a crook named Anthony Sardo into committing crimes. Realizing what he was doing was wrong, the Torch confronted Sardo and during the fight was doused in nitrogen which was the catalyst that allowed him to control his flame from that point on. In Torch's attempting to bring Sardo to justice, the criminal was killed in the battle. When Horton suggested that he and the Torch could use his flame powers to obtain fame and fortune, the Torch rejected this idea leaving Horton's home a flaming inferno which seemingly killed the scientist, however he would resurface later alive and well. In his second recorded adventure, the Human Torch had adopted a human identity and brought Blackie Ross to justice after he had sabotaged a number of race cars. The Torch was helped by a New York City Police officer named Pete Johnson, who became his ally. ===1940s=== thumb|left|The Torch's blue costume of his early adventures In the year 1940, the Human Torch began earning a reputation for himself as a champion of justice. In his third recorded adventure, still confused Human Torch fled New York by train and prevented the crooked Mr. Ritton from exploiting Martians into helping him conquer the world in exchange for TNT to help them fight off invaders to their world. Following that encounter, the Human Torch decided to adopt the name "Jim Hammond" and traveled to New York City. There he found the city under martial law thanks to attacks by Dr. Manyac and his army of Green Flames. The Torch helped defeat Manyac and his minions with the help of his first true ally, police officer Pete Johnson. The Torch soon worked again with Johnson helping recover stolen medical supplies and deliver them to the island community of Orton, also during this time he stopped two crooks named Patch and Turgo from robbing banks in Midtown. After saving the life of an undercover police officer who was discovered by the mobster he was assigned to spy on, the Torch was called a "good guy" for the first time. This prompted him to get Johnson to assist him in getting a job on the New York City police force. Acquiring the job, he was officially sanctioned to use his powers as a police without uniform since they were easily burned away. In his first official case as a police officer, the Torch brought crooked politician Roglo to justice. Becoming lonely, the Human Torch sought out Professor Horton and asked for his advice. Horton told him of asbestos expert Fred Raymond and his wife Nora. Both were terminally ill and raising their son Thomas "Toro" Raymond. Going to visit the Raymond home to learn what Horton was alluding to, the Torch found the Raymond's being terrorized by the criminal Asbestos Lady. The Torch fought off Asbestos Lady and her minions. fields.notes: It has been established that some accounts of the Invaders' wartime exploits were published as comic books and embellished for propaganda purposes. Consequently, certain adventures, particularly those involving the Young Allies, may be fictionalized versions of events rather than entirely reliable historical records. The extent of those alterations remains uncertain. In (12/53, page 4 panel 2) , The Torch says, "You remember, Chief [John Wilson], that I was born in a test tube [a vat is shown] during the last world war..." In (11/91, page 27 panel 2) , Professor Horton is seen growing the Torch in a transparent liquid filled tube as his tendons and muscles are seen because he has no skin and in (7/76, page 6 and panel 3) , is said "Horton, who birthed the Torch inside a huge airtight test-tube". The flashback in showed that the underground lab into which the Mad Thinker descended while carrying the Torch's inert body was in the Nevada desert where the Torch had gone nova in 1955 and implied that it was the same lab that appeared in . However, that cannot be the case since the lab from that annual was later established as being in New York City by the Silver Surfer story in . Therefore, there must have been two labs, one in Nevada and another in New York City.
fields.trivia: According to Wyn, the creation of the original Human Torch is the genesis of Earth-616, referencing . The Human Torch learned to fly before the final confrontation with Tony Sardo, but for some reason didn't use the ability in some of his first adventures. He was still able to run faster than cars and leap over high and broad obstacles. In his first appearance only, the Human Torch had red hair. The Human Torch used to leave burning footprints which were known to have lasted for several hours. The Initiative training facility, Camp Hammond, is named after the Human Torch. Furthermore, a statue of Hammond on the grounds bears the inscription "JIM HAMMOND, THE FIRST OF THE MARVELS: He showed us that heroes can be made." When the camp was shut down by Norman Osborn, an angry mob tore down the statue.

human torch doppelganger.name: Human Torch (Doppelganger)
human torch doppelganger.origin: When the Magus, the dark personality of Adam Warlock, sought to conquer the universe, he first paid a visit to Anthropomorpho in the Dimension of Manifestations to create dopplegangers of every super-hero on Earth. One of these doppelgangers was based off the Fantastic Four's Human Torch. A doppelganger of the Torch was sent to take the place of the original. It attacked Johnny alongside doppelgangers of the X-Men's Cyclops, Storm, Wolverine, Colossus, and Jean Grey. During the fight, the Torch was forced to use his flame powers to kill the Wolverine doppelganger and when he realized that they were mindless creatures, he used his nova flame to slay the rest of the fake X-Men. The doppelganger version of the Torch was more satisfied having compromised the Torch's moral code on killing a foe, and deciding that the original was now as "dark" as his evil shade, the Torch doppelganger teleported away. This or other doppelgangers of the Human Torch were seen during the final battle against the forces of the Magus. Ultimately any remaining dopplegangers of the Torch were apparently destroyed along with all the others when Adam Warlock finally defeated the Magus.

powers: The doppelgangers can assume the form of whatever individual they desire, able to mimic their abilities, powers, and weapons. In their natural form of a tentacled creature, they are able to merge with their prey, taking over their bodies.

human torch ii.origin: ===Early Childhood=== Johnny Storm and his older sister Sue lived uneventfully on Long Island until their mother, Mary Storm, died in an automobile accident. Their father, Doctor Franklin Storm, failed to save her. Despondent, Franklin descended into booze and gambling, eventually winding up in a penitentiary for murder. Sue led Johnny to believe that their father had died rather than let him know that Franklin was in jail. The children went to live with their aunt Marygay. Growing up in suburban Glenville, Johnny Storm was drawn to automobiles despite his mother's death in a car accident, and became quite a mechanic at a young age. Sue spent much of her time looking after Johnny, and while Johnny was a constant source of grief, Johnny cared for his sister and saw her as a surrogate mother. ===The Amulet of Zarathos=== thumb|left|Johnny at 15 At age 15, Johnny's life took a strange turn when Harry Brandeis, a professor of religious studies and father of Sue's friend Cammie, Johnny boyhood crush, was slain while examining the Amulet of Zarathos. Shortly after his death, Johnny sneaked into the Brandeis house to snoop around the crime scene and came into contact with the amulet, which bonded to him as the demon Zarathos sought to make Johnny his Spirit of Vengeance. This made Johnny the target of St. Germaine, who sought to claim the amulet for his master Dracula who was trapped in his Transylvanian castle with a stake in his heart. At Henry's funeral, St. Germaine and his minions went after Johnny, but he was saved thanks to Sue and Henry's brother-in-law Max Parrish, who sought to solve the mystery surrounding his brother-in-law's death. As they sought to learn the secrets behind the Amulet, they were pursued by St. Germaine and his minions, while also being secretly pushed toward the truth by the spirit of Zarathos. Since the Amulet would teleport into Johnny's possession whenever it was taken away from him, the quartet used this to their advantage to keep it away from St. Germaine. However, Sue and Cammy were cornered while trying to escape from their foe. At that point, Zarathos appeared before Johnny and told him of his intentions to make him the new Spirit of Vengeance. In order to save Sue and Cammy's lives, Johnny agreed to become the vessel for Zarathos, but before he could be possessed by the demon, Max grabbed the amulet, becoming the Ghost Rider instead. As Ghost Rider, Max destroyed St. Germaine, and struggled for control over Zarathos until Johnny ripped the Amulet from his makeshift motorcycle, restoring Max to normal. They then tossed the Amulet in a junk yard where they hoped it would not be found. After this adventure, Sue decided to go to Hollywood and pursue a career in acting. Johnny spent his high school years attending Glenville High, during his junior year Johnny was briefly tormented by David George Munson. Johnny also attempted to use his prowess with mechanics to build a hot rod to try and gain popularity. However his attempts to pick up girls was thwarted by the athletic Mike Snow, the schools star wrestler. Johnny was frequently in trouble with school administration who feared that he didn't take his education seriously. ===Birth of the Fantastic Four=== thumb|right|Johnny Storm first flaming on When Johnny was 16, he followed his sister to Central City, California. By this time, Sue was the fiancée of scientist Reed Richards who had been developing a rocket that operated on a hyper-drive technology. However, just as the Reed neared completion of the rocket, the government pulled the plug. Reed was determined to fly the rocket before the government could shut him down; Reed's pilot Ben Grimm warned that the ship wasn't properly shielded against radiation, but Reed pressed along anyway. Not wishing Reed to go alone, Sue insisted on coming along. Reed planned to embark on a mission on the first faster-than-light rocketship to reach an Earthlike planet called Spyre located 44 lightyears away. After looking through the advanced scanner that Reed used to find this planet, Johnny was overcome by an impulse to join the mission, feeling that something was waiting for him out there. Johnny pushed himself through strenuous training and became the youngest pilot in NASA. While originally enlisted as backup pilot, Johnny joined Reed, Sue and Ben Grimm on an unauthorized space flight aboard the Marvel-1. While the rocket launch was a complete success, while passing through the their ship was bombarded with cosmic rays, causing the rocket to crash land back on Earth. Each member of the crew was mutated by the cosmic rays and endowed with fantastic powers. Reed gained the ability to stretch his now mailable body, Sue gained the ability to turn invisible, and Ben turned into a monstrous thing. Johnny meanwhile gained the ability to burst into flame. Johnny decided to name himself the Human Torch, after the similarly powered hero from World War II. Reed convinced the group to use their powers for

Their father, Doctor Franklin Storm, failed to save her. Despondent, Franklin descended into booze and gambling, eventually winding up in a penitentiary for murder. Sue led Johnny to believe that their father had died rather than let him know that Franklin was in jail. The children went to live with their aunt Marygay. Growing up in suburban Glenville, Johnny Storm was drawn to automobiles despite his mother's death in a car accident, and became quite a mechanic at a young age. Sue spent much of her time looking after Johnny, and while Johnny was a constant source of grief, Johnny cared for his sister and saw her as a surrogate mother. ===The Amulet of Zarathos=== thumb|left|Johnny at 15 At age 15, Johnny's life took a strange turn when Harry Brandeis, a professor of religious studies and father of Sue's friend Cammie, Johnny boyhood crush, was slain while examining the Amulet of Zarathos. Shortly after his death, Johnny sneaked into the Brandeis house to snoop around the crime scene and came into contact with the amulet, which bonded to him as the demon Zarathos sought to make Johnny his Spirit of Vengeance. This made Johnny the target of St. Germaine, who sought to claim the amulet for his master Dracula who was trapped in his Transylvanian castle with a stake in his heart. At Henry's funeral, St. Germaine and his minions went after Johnny, but he was saved thanks to Sue and Henry's brother-in-law Max Parrish, who sought to solve the mystery surrounding his brother-in-law's death. As they sought to learn the secrets behind the Amulet, they were pursued by St. Germaine and his minions, while also being secretly pushed toward the truth by the spirit of Zarathos. Since the Amulet would teleport into Johnny's possession whenever it was taken away from him, the quartet used this to their advantage to keep it away from St. Germaine. However, Sue and Cammy were cornered while trying to escape from their foe. At that point, Zarathos appeared before Johnny and told him of his intentions to make him the new Spirit of Vengeance. In order to save Sue and Cammy's lives, Johnny agreed to become the vessel for Zarathos, but before he could be possessed by the demon, Max grabbed the amulet, becoming the Ghost Rider instead. As Ghost Rider, Max destroyed St. Germaine, and struggled for control over Zarathos until Johnny ripped the Amulet from his makeshift motorcycle, restoring Max to normal. They then tossed the Amulet in a junk yard where they hoped it would not be found. After this adventure, Sue decided to go to Hollywood and pursue a career in acting. Johnny spent his high school years attending Glenville High, during his junior year Johnny was briefly tormented by David George Munson. Johnny also attempted to use his prowess with mechanics to build a hot rod to try and gain popularity. However his attempts to pick up girls was thwarted by the athletic Mike Snow, the schools star wrestler. Johnny was frequently in trouble with school administration who feared that he didn't take his education seriously. ===Birth of the Fantastic Four=== thumb|right|Johnny Storm first flaming on When Johnny was 16, he followed his sister to Central City, California. By this time, Sue was the fiancée of scientist Reed Richards who had been developing a rocket that operated on a hyper-drive technology. However, just as the Reed neared completion of the rocket, the government pulled the plug. Reed was determined to fly the rocket before the government could shut him down; Reed's pilot Ben Grimm warned that the ship wasn't properly shielded against radiation, but Reed pressed along anyway. Not wishing Reed to go alone, Sue insisted on coming along. Reed planned to embark on a mission on the first faster-than-light rocketship to reach an Earthlike planet called Spyre located 44 lightyears away. After looking through the advanced scanner that Reed used to find this planet, Johnny was overcome by an impulse to join the mission, feeling that something was waiting for him out there. Johnny pushed himself through strenuous training and became the youngest pilot in NASA. While originally enlisted as backup pilot, Johnny joined Reed, Sue and Ben Grimm on an unauthorized space flight aboard the Marvel-1. While the rocket launch was a complete success, while passing through the their ship was bombarded with cosmic rays, causing the rocket to crash land back on Earth. Each member of the crew was mutated by the cosmic rays and endowed with fantastic powers. Reed gained the ability to stretch his now mailable body, Sue gained the ability to turn invisible, and Ben turned into a monstrous thing. Johnny meanwhile gained the ability to burst into flame. Johnny decided to name himself the Human Torch, after the similarly powered hero from World War II. Reed convinced the group to use their powers for
fields.personality: ===Relationships=== Johnny has been in relationships with: Dorrie Evans, Crystal, Frankie Raye, Zsaji, Lyja, Namorita, Kourtney Keaton, Darla Deering, Psionics, Rogue, Medusa, Sky, and Angelica of the Shore, among many other shorter relationships.
powers: only when the Human Torch wills his flame to a higher level does the majority of surplus energy with the AR-HP complex become involved. In its plasma state, The Torch's body is no longer solid
fields.notes: In 2016, writer Marjorie Liu confirmed Johnny and Daken were intentionally written with sexual tension in due to her belief that they previously had a physical relationship. Whether or not this was meant to be a result of Daken's pheromones powers, or Johnny being written as bisexual was not clarified.
fields.trivia: The powers of all of the Fantastic Four are based on one of the four elements, with Johnny's element being fire. Since Johnny burns off any dirt or germs in his body when he flames on, he hasn't had the actual need to brush his teeth or take a shower since he gained his powers. thumb|right|Johnny's infamous song In from the 1994 cartoon, Johnny sings an original song that became rather infamous in real life and it is sometimes joked about in the comics. Johnny is said to be the best singer of the Fantastic Four, with "the voice of an angel," and the song from the cartoon is his ringtone. Johnny drinks his tea black, with three sugars. After his nephew Franklin dyed his hair black, Johnny approved of it, stating "We've got enough blondes in this family." While working on a 1957 T-Bird, Wolverine noted that Johnny smelled like Dr. Brandt and motor oil, and was chewing . The Human Torch was one of the characters featured in Series A of the Marvel Value Stamps issued in the 1970's.

humanoid experimental robot b type integ.origin: ===Origin=== Mister Fantastic found himself in need of a robot utilizing advanced Xandarian technology, so he sought to collaborate with Master Xar of the Xandarians. Inspired by the earlier cartoon portrayal, he decided to model this new creation after the animated H.E.R.B.I.E. The Fantastic Four, embarking on a quest to locate Galactus for aid against the Sphinx, hoped that H.E.R.B.I.E. would prove instrumental in their search. However, unbeknownst to them, the villain Doctor Sun had infiltrated H.E.R.B.I.E.'s body, harboring his consciousness within. Despite initial suspicions from the Thing, they pressed on, encountering the Slig race along their journey. A confrontation ensued, resulting in the demise of a Slig criminal, Krogg, at the hands of H.E.R.B.I.E., manipulated under Dr. Sun's influence. Continuing their voyage, H.E.R.B.I.E. guided the Fantastic Four to Galactus's domain. There, Galactus tasked them, along with H.E.R.B.I.E., with finding a new herald. The chosen individual, Tyros, was transformed into the formidable Terrax the Tamer. Amidst the intense conflict between the Fantastic Four, Terrax, and Galactus in defense of Earth, H.E.R.B.I.E. fell under Doctor Sun 's sway once more. Manipulated, it commenced the construction of a duplicate Ultimate Nullifier. This potent weapon ultimately became a pivotal tool for Mr. Fantastic, who cunningly employed it to deceive Galactus into withdrawing from Earth's vicinity. Driven by Doctor Sun 's influence, H.E.R.B.I.E. unleashed Blastaar from the confines of the Negative Zone, aiming to annihilate the Fantastic Four. However, Blastaar's efforts proved futile, and the villain's scheme ultimately faltered. Doctor Sun resumed control over H.E.R.B.I.E., launching a vicious assault on the Fantastic Four. Employing the defenses of the Baxter Building, he incapacitated both the Invisible Girl and Human Torch, while also overpowering Mr. Fantastic and the Thing in combat. Seizing the opportunity, Dr. Sun abandoned H.E.R.B.I.E.'s physical form to infiltrate the Baxter Building's master computer, seizing control of the entire facility. Despite Mr. Fantastic's efforts to contain him, Dr. Sun's threat persisted, prompting H.E.R.B.I.E. to make the ultimate sacrifice. Recognizing the danger posed by Dr. Sun's potential return, H.E.R.B.I.E. chose to selflessly hurl itself into the master computer, annihilating both itself and Dr. Sun to ensure the safety of the Fantastic Four. In a humorous turn of events, the Human Torch orchestrated an April Fool's prank on the Thing involving a colossal H.E.R.B.I.E. replica. However, his miscalculation led to the prank occurring on March 31st instead. Amused by the error, the Thing humorously reminded the Torch of the mnemonic "Thirty days has September...", prompting the Torch to promptly end the prank. When Luke Cage and Iron Fist, accompanied by Rom, launched an incursion into the Baxter Building out of concern that the Fantastic Four had been supplanted by Dire Wraiths, they encountered a squad of H.E.R.B.I.E. robots. In the ensuing skirmish, Luke Cage and Iron Fist engaged in combat with the robots, while Rom took decisive action by disabling the building's main computer. This strategic move caused the H.E.R.B.I.E. units to cease their assault. Reed Richards extended a gesture of support to Tony Stark's latest venture in Los Angeles by dispatching H.E.R.B.I.E. with a substantial financial contribution in the form of a large check. Sue Storm tasked H.E.R.B.I.E. with reminding Reed about an upcoming charity event that the Fantastic Four were scheduled to attend. However, Reed utilized a binary code override to deactivate H.E.R.B.I.E., effectively dismissing the reminder. The Reanimator acquired a H.E.R.B.I.E. unit, employing it to surveil the superhero Nova. During fight against Condor in Reed Richard's laboratory, a H.E.R.B.I.E. unit sprang into action, deploying its extinguisher foam to combat the spreading flames. In his exploration of Weirdworld, Black Knight stumbled upon a dormant H.E.R.B.I.E. unit. ===Cage McKnight=== H.E.R.B.I.E. 1.05 landed a role as the sound mixer in a movie produced by "Cage McKnight," who was later revealed to be Mysterio in disguise. Throughout the production, H.E.R.B.I.E. collaborated with actress Mary Jane Watson, production manager Screwball, and director of photography Master Matrix. As filming progressed, H.E.R.B.I.E. continued to fulfill his duties as the sound technician. When the Savage Six launched an attack on the movie set, H.E.R.B.I.E. found himself standing alongside Master Matrix, "Cage McKnight," Screwball, Kangaroo, Mallorie, and Sonny Diperna in defense against the assailants. ===Doctor Doom=== When suspicions arose regarding Dr. Doom's involvement in a terrorist act targeting the Antlion project a black hole device intended to mitigate climate change the Fantastic Four deployed a larger, human-sized H.E.R.B.I.E. unit to oversee the unfolding events. fields.notes: H.E.R.B.I.E. was an original character created for 's 1978 Fantastic Four animated series to replace the Human Torch. Around this time, Marvel had licensed a number of their characters to to develop live-action TV movies and series, one of them being the Human Torch. With use of the Human Torch restricted because of that, his place in the Fantastic Four was taken by H.E.R.B.I.E., who was conceived and named by Stan Lee and designed by Jack Kirby. A year later, H.E.R.B.I.E. made the jump to the comics.
fields.trivia: Shortly after the Fantastic Four cartoon premiered in the 1970's, the little robot was introduced to the comics continuity by writer Marv Wolfman and artist John Byrne. As within the Marvel Universe, with the Fantastic Four have marketed their likenesses for a successful in-universe comic series, H.E.R.B.I.E.'s physical appearance was likewise explained as being based on the animated series based on that comic. H.E.R.B.I.E. had a crush on Roberta, another robot created by Richards.

Inspired by the earlier cartoon portrayal, he decided to model this new creation after the animated H.E.R.B.I.E. The Fantastic Four, embarking on a quest to locate Galactus for aid against the Sphinx, hoped that H.E.R.B.I.E. would prove instrumental in their search. However, unbeknownst to them, the villain Doctor Sun had infiltrated H.E.R.B.I.E.'s body, harboring his consciousness within. Despite initial suspicions from the Thing, they pressed on, encountering the Slig race along their journey. A confrontation ensued, resulting in the demise of a Slig criminal, Krogg, at the hands of H.E.R.B.I.E., manipulated under Dr. Sun's influence. Continuing their voyage, H.E.R.B.I.E. guided the Fantastic Four to Galactus's domain. There, Galactus tasked them, along with H.E.R.B.I.E., with finding a new herald. The chosen individual, Tyros, was transformed into the formidable Terrax the Tamer. Amidst the intense conflict between the Fantastic Four, Terrax, and Galactus in defense of Earth, H.E.R.B.I.E. fell under Doctor Sun 's sway once more. Manipulated, it commenced the construction of a duplicate Ultimate Nullifier. This potent weapon ultimately became a pivotal tool for Mr. Fantastic, who cunningly employed it to deceive Galactus into withdrawing from Earth's vicinity. Driven by Doctor Sun 's influence, H.E.R.B.I.E. unleashed Blastaar from the confines of the Negative Zone, aiming to annihilate the Fantastic Four. However, Blastaar's efforts proved futile, and the villain's scheme ultimately faltered. Doctor Sun resumed control over H.E.R.B.I.E., launching a vicious assault on the Fantastic Four. Employing the defenses of the Baxter Building, he incapacitated both the Invisible Girl and Human Torch, while also overpowering Mr. Fantastic and the Thing in combat. Seizing the opportunity, Dr. Sun abandoned H.E.R.B.I.E.'s physical form to infiltrate the Baxter Building's master computer, seizing control of the entire facility. Despite Mr. Fantastic's efforts to contain him, Dr. Sun's threat persisted, prompting H.E.R.B.I.E. to make the ultimate sacrifice. Recognizing the danger posed by Dr. Sun's potential return, H.E.R.B.I.E. chose to selflessly hurl itself into the master computer, annihilating both itself and Dr. Sun to ensure the safety of the Fantastic Four. In a humorous turn of events, the Human Torch orchestrated an April Fool's prank on the Thing involving a colossal H.E.R.B.I.E. replica. However, his miscalculation led to the prank occurring on March 31st instead. Amused by the error, the Thing humorously reminded the Torch of the mnemonic "Thirty days has September...", prompting the Torch to promptly end the prank. When Luke Cage and Iron Fist, accompanied by Rom, launched an incursion into the Baxter Building out of concern that the Fantastic Four had been supplanted by Dire Wraiths, they encountered a squad of H.E.R.B.I.E. robots. In the ensuing skirmish, Luke Cage and Iron Fist engaged in combat with the robots, while Rom took decisive action by disabling the building's main computer. This strategic move caused the H.E.R.B.I.E. units to cease their assault. Reed Richards extended a gesture of support to Tony Stark's latest venture in Los Angeles by dispatching H.E.R.B.I.E. with a substantial financial contribution in the form of a large check. Sue Storm tasked H.E.R.B.I.E. with reminding Reed about an upcoming charity event that the Fantastic Four were scheduled to attend. However, Reed utilized a binary code override to deactivate H.E.R.B.I.E., effectively dismissing the reminder. The Reanimator acquired a H.E.R.B.I.E. unit, employing it to surveil the superhero Nova. During fight against Condor in Reed Richard's laboratory, a H.E.R.B.I.E. unit sprang into action, deploying its extinguisher foam to combat the spreading flames. In his exploration of Weirdworld, Black Knight stumbled upon a dormant H.E.R.B.I.E. unit. ===Cage McKnight=== H.E.R.B.I.E. 1.05 landed a role as the sound mixer in a movie produced by "Cage McKnight," who was later revealed to be Mysterio in disguise. Throughout the production, H.E.R.B.I.E. collaborated with actress Mary Jane Watson, production manager Screwball, and director of photography Master Matrix. As filming progressed, H.E.R.B.I.E. continued to fulfill his duties as the sound technician. When the Savage Six launched an attack on the movie set, H.E.R.B.I.E. found himself standing alongside Master Matrix, "Cage McKnight," Screwball, Kangaroo, Mallorie, and Sonny Diperna in defense against the assailants. ===Doctor Doom=== When suspicions arose regarding Dr. Doom's involvement in a terrorist act targeting the Antlion project a black hole device intended to mitigate climate change the Fantastic Four deployed a larger, human-sized H.E.R.B.I.E. unit to oversee the unfolding events. fields.notes: H.E.R.B.I.E. was an original character created for 's 1978 Fantastic Four animated series to replace the Human Torch. Around this time, Marvel had licensed a number of their characters to to develop live-action TV movies and series, one of them being the Human Torch. With use of the Human Torch restricted because of that, his place in the Fantastic Four was taken by H.E.R.B.I.E., who was conceived and named by Stan Lee and designed by Jack Kirby. A year later, H.E.R.B.I.E. made the jump to the comics.
fields.trivia: Shortly after the Fantastic Four cartoon premiered in the 1970's, the little robot was introduced to the comics continuity by writer Marv Wolfman and artist John Byrne. As within the Marvel Universe, with the Fantastic Four have marketed their likenesses for a successful in-universe comic series, H.E.R.B.I.E.'s physical appearance was likewise explained as being based on the animated series based on that comic. H.E.R.B.I.E. had a crush on Roberta, another robot created by Richards.

He has not been seen since then and it is unknown if he left the Morlocks or, if he stayed, survived Mikhail Rasputin's flooding of the Morlock tunnels. If he is still alive, whether swept away or not, it is unknown if kept his mutant powers or not after M-Day. ===Reign of X=== He reappeared with his brother and the Morlocks to defend Lowtown in Madripoor from the attacking Reavers.

humphrey bogart.name: Humphrey Bogart
humphrey bogart.origin: Humphrey Bogart was a well-known actor in films in the 1940s and 50s. He died of cancer in 1957. However, many years later, he was seen in the Laughing Horse bar in Manhattan. ===Legacy=== Floyd Donahue, a Skrull from Kral IV, chose to maintain the form of Humphrey Bogart as he appeared in the film . The Minotaur-like sorcerer Rintrah would often use his magic to take the form of his favorite actor Humphrey Bogart.

hungan.species: Human, a witch doctor from a small tribe of Kenyans
hungan.origin: Hungan was an African witch doctor who once was worshipped by a small tribe of Kenyans. He reigned over the tribe until Storm drove him out, and was proclaimed the tribe's Goddess. Ten years later Hungan regained control of the tribe after Storm joined the X-Men, but sought revenge against her for being usurped initially. Hungan and his elite tribesman arrive at the X-Mansion, escaping with Storm as his prisoner. He confined Storm in a small box, triggering her severe claustrophobia in the process. Hungan captured her will (possibly meaning her soul) into his sceptre, giving him the ability to control her body. The X-Men eventually located Hungan and his tribesmen but he used the mind-controlled Storm to attack them. Storm's nephew, Spyke used his powers to shatter the crystal atop Hungan's scepter, releasing Storm from his control. Angrily, Storm engulfed the Hungan in a force of wind that threw him into the sea. Afterwards Hungan's tribe disappeared into the mist.

hunger devourer of realities.name: Hunger (Devourer of Realities)
hunger devourer of realities.origin: Hunger was a universal-scale parasite that lived outside of the known universe, within the great Cosmic Vortex. It fed on whole realities. When the Infinity Gauntlet was first assembled, it brought Earth-616 to the attention of Hunger, who sought to devour it, as has supposedly happened with many other realities in the past. However, the nature of this reality required that someone within it created a hole for Hunger to gain entrance. Hunger manipulated the technology and thoughts of Galactus to convince him that the Infinity Gems could permanently end his need for the energy of living planets. Upon gathering the Gems from inside and outside the universe, Galactus assembled them in a crux that instead opened a gateway to the Vortex, allowing Hunger into Earth-616. Thanos intervened, destroying the gateway and scattering the Gems across the universe again. However, a very small portion of Hunger was left alive within Thanos' reality. A time-traveling Adam Warlock later used the original Soul Gem to secretly encourage Hunger to find a way to get his revenge on Thanos. In the year 2127 of an alternate timeline, Hunger infected the inhabitants of planet Zelchia and in the year 4657 battled a near-omnipotent Thanos. Despite having absorbed the entirety of the cosmic beings, Thanos was ultimately destroyed by Hunger. However, a time-traveling omnipotent Thanos took control of his past self and killed Hunger before it could infect the people of Zelchia in 2127, thus preventing his own defeat.

fields.notes: In , the Defenders travel back to the Third Cosmos and help destroy the Anti-All, a primordial manifestation of nothingness. When the creature is shattered into seemingly one piece for every universe, Doctor Strange theorizes that when heroes fight against "the great Nothing" in their own times, they're fighting back the Anti-All as well. This could mean that a being like Hunger could have been born out of the Anti-All's fracture.

hunger extraterrestrial.name: Hunger (Extraterrestrial)
hunger extraterrestrial.origin: After failing to command the power of Aron the Rogue Watcher Doctor Doom sought to exploit the energies of another alien creature by drawing it to Earth using a space probe. What he drew to Earth and his native Latveria was a creature who was later called the Hunger. Upon its arrival it began travelling across the Latverian countryside, consuming the energies of the various soldiers, robots and civilians it crossed paths with. It eventually took possession of a soldier's body and used it as a physical form to attack Castle Doom. Inside it clashed with various Doombots until Doctor Doom came to steal the Hunger's energies. Although the Hunger destroyed the device, it was fought back by the Fantastic Four's Thing, who was Doom's prisoner at the time. The Thing then plunged exposed wires into the animated corpse causes enough energy feedback to create an explosion. This coincided with the arrival of the rest of the Fantastic Four who recovered both the Thing and Doctor Doom from the rubble while the Hunger got away. Back in the countryside, the Hunger had gathered enough energy to assume a physical form. The Fantastic Four and their allies Psi-Lord and Lyja tried to contain the creature while Mister Fantastic and Doctor Doom developed a means of teleporting the creature back out into deep space using Doom's Matter Transference Device. During the final attack, the Hunger was winning the battle having fought off all his opponents. Seeing that this could mean the demise of his people, Doom put on a battery pack containing the last of the energies stolen from Aron to battle the Hunger one-on-one. Doom drained the last of this power and was seriously injured in a retaliatory blast. Although this gave the Hunger pause long enough for Doom to activate the Matter Transference device and banish the Hunger to the deepest regions of space. The Hunger's subsequent fate is unknown.

hungry.species: Possible demonic entity or possible primal mutant
hungry.first_appearance: Heroes for Hope Starring the X-Men Vol 1 1
hungry.origin: The entity known as Hungry is ancient. It has been speculated that it is a primal mutant that evolved alongside humanity, feeding on suffering and misery. In ancient times, it came to reside in Africa, where the local people tried to drive it out. Failing, they erected a temple to try and appease it. In the modern era, it became aware of the emergence of mutants, and decided both to test the 'flavor' of their misery and to determine whether they were a possible threat to its own existence. It used illusions to torment the X-Men, exposing them to their greatest subconscious fears: Colossus being mocked by steely, apparitions of the team. Next, Shadowcat encountered her fear of starvation, with Hungry tormenting Kitty with a seemingly delicious meal, only to render it to insects while briefly rendering the poor girl to skin and bones. Following this, Nightcrawler ends up believing himself a coward after facing his own illusion, focusing on Christian imagery and moral dilemmas, in which he refuses to sacrifice himself so another person could breathe the air and eat the food he would. Meanwhile Magneto is next with being shown a glimpse of his dream of mutant supremacy, only to see it isn't as glorious as he'd envisioned it. Phoenix follows, being taken back to her past, confronted by a hoard of mutant hunting doppelgängers Hounds, reminding her of that part of her terrible future while Wolverine is made to try and confront the tension between his animal and human halves. However, when it confronted Storm, Hungry found it couldn't break her will so easily like it had with the others, and she successfully rallied her comrades, while Phoenix helped them identify the source of the psychic attacks. At its home in Africa, the X-Men found the local population stricken by famine. Although Hungry had not caused the famine directly, it had fed on the local people's suffering and pain. That night, Rogue, who had absorbed the powers of the other X-Men, confronted Hungry at its temple. Her attempt to absorb it backfired, and instead Hungry took possession of her body. When the other X-Men awoke, they confronted Hungry, and eventually were able to drive it from Rogue and destroy its temple. However, the entity was not truly destroyed, and the X-Men theorized it could not truly be defeated as long as human suffering existed.

hungry charlie.name: Hungry Charlie
hungry charlie.origin: Hungry Charlie was a homeless man who lived on the Bowery. When he met Namor, he asked him if he knew Sunshine Mary and Charlie said that everyone knew her and would have taken him to her, but instead he led to an ambush carried out by other homeless people thinking that he was one of those who were making the members of the Bowery community disappear. The Sub-Mariner made easy play of the homeless and learned of the kidnappings, including that of Sunshine Mary. After learning where the homeless were being taken, The Sub-Mariner had himself taken to that place accompanied by Hungry Charlie and the entire Bowery community. The location was a secret A.I.M. laboratory and the homeless were used as guinea pigs to experiment with the Virus X created by MODOK. Among the guinea pigs there was also a captured Thing who freed himself and together with the Sub-Mariner faced the A.I.M. androids, while Hungry Charlie and the other homeless faced the A.I.M. members and they freed their friends.

hungry one.name: Hungry One
hungry one.species: Pre- or early human born different from his kind
hungry one.origin: ===Origin=== Born different, "This One" at some point revealed itself to his fellows, urging them to kill him. Running across the caves, he managed to hide from behind a waterfall. Remaining hidden for a very long time, This One's hunger finally faded, his body devolved into an amorphous blob until he found a new source of food: sound. ===Modern Age=== When the waterfall became silent, he moved and hid into an old deserted house, and when hippies Denny and Sheila went into it, Denny stuck his leg into the rotten floor, allowing This One to feed upon their hysterical reactions. They managed to flee and Denny thought of reaching to a place where there would be less environmental sound, starving This One. It is unknown if Sheila, under panic, finally screamed (giving him the strength he needed to go on) or not. Allegedly, only her headshrinker knew the outcome.

hunk larken.name: Hunk Larken
hunk larken.origin: Hunk Larken was always considered an outsider due to his large size and great strength. He tried to become a professional athlete but proved too slow and clumsy for the games of basketball, baseball and boxing. Hungry and alone, Hunk took a job in a travelling carnival as a sideshow attraction called the Modern Monstrosity. He was fired from the carnival when he attacked a spectator who made derogatory comments about him. Once again down on his luck, Hunk applied to be a test subject for a mission to Outer Space. Accepted because of his strength and low nervous response, Hunk was sent out into space in an early form of spacecraft. Upon reaching outer space, the ship passed through a cloud of unknown radioactive anti-matter which penetrated the ship's hull and nearly killed Larken. Hunk, however, had managed to bring the spacecraft back to Earth in the nick of time and, upon inspection, it was found that he had gained unusual powers from his exposure to the anti-matter. By lifting his left arm, Hunk could attract all objects and people towards him and could repel them just as quickly by raising his right arm. Hunk immediately realized that with his newfound powers, he could strike back at a world that had mocked and ridiculed him for his entire life. Dubbed Magnetor by the public, Larken went on a rampage, first destroying the carnival where he had worked, then robbing a back and finally by pulling down an entire building. He even repelled incoming jet fighters that were trying to destroy him. A short time later, however, Larken realized that his powers were wearing off and were not inexhaustible as he had first believed. Hunted as a fugitive, Larken hid for days until he sneaked back to the space research facility and boarded another spacecraft. After the automated ship had left Earth's atmosphere, a voice came through the speakers informing Larken that they knew who he was and why he had gone on such a rampage. They told him that they had built this ship especially for him and that contained years worth of food. They told him that they wished him to find the happiness that had always been denied him on Earth. With a tear in his eye, a thankful Larken piloted the ship into the great unknown. His current whereabouts and subsequent history are unknown.

hunter.species: Human mutated by the Dimension Z into a Werewolf
hunter.origin: ===Adoption=== thumb|left|250px|The king's son When a plane crashed outside the northern border of the remote African nation Wakanda, the King T'Chaka when to scanning the wreckage and found a white infant boy, all other passengers dead. The monarch astounded his people by adopting the child as his son with his wife N'Yami. T'Chaka named his son Hunter, and although he was viewed with suspicion due to his status as an outsider, he had a princely upbringing, learning combat and hunting at his father's side. However, Hunter's status in the family shifted after, T'Chaka's wife, N'Yami, died giving birth to her son, T'Challa. Hunter resented his new brother for his beloved foster mother's death, a feeling that intensified when he realized that T'Challa was T'Chaka's favoured one and heir apparent. However, Hunter found a kindred spirit in Ramonda, T'Chaka's South Africa second wife, and the two bonded over their shared status as relative outsiders to Wakanda. They became as close as mother and son. thumb|right|300px|One race of many between brothers Nevertheless, in their youths, T'Challa and Hunter were close, and would compete in childish games like footraces, but Hunter soon really became jealous of his brother, the way everyone was speaking of him like he was already the Black Panther, feeling past over and lost the chance to prove himself. When the family visited South Africa to honor Ramonda's deceased mother, the country's apartheid segregation policy forced him to separate from his brother and parents, which fueled his feelings of otherness. thumb|left|250px|The royal family in grief During a ceremony held in the border of Wakanda, T'Chaka was approached by physicist Ulysses Klaw, who attempted to petition for the mining rights of the nation's rare metal called Vibranium. Klaw was backed up by a group of mercenaries, who opened fire as soon as T'Chaka refused. Blaming T'Challa for the death of their father as well because T'Chaka had died shielding T'Challa from Klaw's attack. He also blamed himself, believing he should have seen Klaw coming and executed him before he ever became a problem. Not long afterwards, Ramonda was also kidnapped back to South Africa by Anton Pretorius, leaving Hunter orphaned for a second time. ===The White Wolf=== thumb|right|300px|Hunter as White Wolf with his loyal dogs Before his father death, when Hunter was old enough, his father placed him in charge of the Hatut Zeraze ("Dogs of War"), Wakanda's secret police and became known as the White Wolf. As Chieftain, he carefully choose his own men, and as part of initiation to become a member of the Hatut Zeraze, he would branded any man's cheeks to mark him as a Hatut Zeraze for the rest of life. Some of the Hatut Zeraze, such as Derek Khanata, was hesitant to leave because the White Wolf horrifically punished deserters. Hunter was devoted to his father and his adoptive country. He carried out his duties of protecting Wakanda from its enemies both foreign and domestic, doing whatever it took to get the job done. Often employing political prisoners, kidnapping, torture, brutality and assassination. Hunter's white complexion was also a boon to the Wakandan royal family, though, and T'Chaka would send him on missions to places overseas that were easier for Europeans to access. ===The Oromo Conflict=== After their father's passing T'Challa went on walkabout throughout Africa, and their uncle the regent S'Yan empower Hunter and the Hatut Zeraze even further to maintain peace. Believing that Wakanda would be strengthened if other countries in its vicinity were weakened, Hunter used the Hatut Zeraze to cause unrest in neighboring countries, including Ethiopia. One of them, the Oromo Conflict, wreaked havoc on Ethiopia and, among many other calamities, caused many young Ethiopians to lose their homes, and be forced to migrate on foot to nearby countries; all of Ethiopia's neighbouring countries accepted refugees from the Oromo Conflict, except Wakanda, that insisted on its pledge not to intervene in the affairs of other nations. He also used his secret police force to keep T'Challa in exile. If T'Challa couldn't come home, he couldn't continue his plan to open Wakanda, which Hunter blames for their father's death. Believing that his brother would make a weak ruler of Wakanda, Hunter even attempted to prevent T'Challa from competing in the Tournament for the throne: however, with their sister Shuri's help, he was thwarted, and T'Challa ascended to the throne. ===Still in Service=== Although his relationship with his brother began to deteriorate due to their differing visions for Wakanda, Hunter, still Chieftain of the Hatut Zeraze, continued to fulfill the role his father had entrusted to him. Hunter resented his new brother for his beloved foster mother's death, a feeling that intensified when he realized that T'Challa was T'Chaka's favoured one and heir apparent. However, Hunter found a kindred spirit in Ramonda, T'Chaka's South Africa second wife, and the two bonded over their shared status as relative outsiders to Wakanda. They became as close as mother and son. thumb|right|300px|One race of many between brothers Nevertheless, in their youths, T'Challa and Hunter were close, and would compete in childish games like footraces, but Hunter soon really became jealous of his brother, the way everyone was speaking of him like he was already the Black Panther, feeling past over and lost the chance to prove himself. Klaw was backed up by a group of mercenaries, who opened fire as soon as T'Chaka refused. Blaming T'Challa for the death of their father as well because T'Chaka had died shielding T'Challa from Klaw's attack. He also blamed himself, believing he should have seen Klaw coming and executed him before he ever became a problem. Not long afterwards, Ramonda was also kidnapped back to South Africa by Anton Pretorius, leaving Hunter orphaned for a second time. ===The White Wolf=== thumb|right|300px|Hunter as White Wolf with his loyal dogs Before his father death, when Hunter was old enough, his father placed him in charge of the Hatut Zeraze ("Dogs of War"), Wakanda's secret police and became known as the White Wolf. As Chieftain, he carefully choose his own men, and as part of initiation to become a member of the Hatut Zeraze, he would branded any man's cheeks to mark him as a Hatut Zeraze for the rest of life. Some of the Hatut Zeraze, such as Derek Khanata, was hesitant to leave because the White Wolf horrifically punished deserters. Hunter was devoted to his father and his adoptive country. He carried out his duties of protecting Wakanda from its enemies both foreign and domestic, doing whatever it took to get the job done. Often employing political prisoners, kidnapping, torture, brutality and assassination. Hunter's white complexion was also a boon to the Wakandan royal family, though, and T'Chaka would send him on missions to places overseas that were easier for Europeans to access. ===The Oromo Conflict=== After their father's passing T'Challa went on walkabout throughout Africa, and their uncle the regent S'Yan empower Hunter and the Hatut Zeraze even further to maintain peace. Believing that Wakanda would be strengthened if other countries in its vicinity were weakened, Hunter used the Hatut Zeraze to cause unrest in neighboring countries, including Ethiopia. hunter pride.name: Hunter (Pride)
hunter pride.origin: Hunter was one of Alex Wilder's friends who played a Marvel heroes themed MMORPG along with Stretch, Oscar, and Lotus. He was a skilled hacker and eBay auctioneer with an antiauthoritarian attitude. After Alex's death, Hunter covertly researched Alex and the Pride. Believing the Alex and the Pride were the "good guys", the group used the Abstract to cast a spell to retrieve Alex from the past before he died. During the ceremony, Oscar died and a young Geoffrey Wilder was summoned to the present instead of Alex. 200px|thumb|left|Hunter hacking into the Leapfrog (Vehicle)|Leapfrog Thinking they could still honor Alex's memory and save the world, Hunter, Stretch, and Lotus formed the New Pride. Using magical items from the Minorus, the New Pride began to covertly gather information about the Runaways. When they directly confronted the Runaways, they kidnapped Molly Hayes not knowing that Geoffrey planned to sacrifice her to the Gibborim. During the rescue, Geoffrey seemingly murdered Gertrude Yorkes leading to the disbanding of the New Pride. Following Gert's death, Lotus returned to her day job and Stretch checked himself into a mental health facility while Hunter joined the Peace Corps to atone for the "blood" on his hands.

hunter brawn.name: Hunter Brawn
hunter brawn.origin: Hunter Brawn was a shady businessman who was laundering lots of money through a bank. When the president of the bank found out what was happening, he threatened Brawn to go to the police, so, that night, Brawn arranged for both the president and his wife to be killed in an automobile "accident". The Bank president and his wife were actually the parents of future X-Man Jubilee and, many years later, Jubilee finally brought Mr. Brawn to justice with the help of her Gen X teammates.

hunter in darkness.name: Hunter in Darkness
hunter in darkness.species: Possibly "the last of his Lupine kind"
hunter in darkness.origin: The Hunter in Darkness was the subject of legends among the Blackfoot tribe. Years ago, the creature had been caught in a steel bear trap. Wolverine, in a feral state after escaping the Weapon X program, freed the Hunter. Years later, the Hunter in Darkness encountered him again. The hero was searching the Canadian wilderness for an escaped fugitive, Athabasca Ike. The Hunter attacked and fought Wolverine, until Ike shot it. The creature recovered, killed Ike, and then escaped. Some time later, the Hunter in Darkness was captured by casino owner Ronald Parvenue. It was put on display in a cage suspended from Parvenue's helicopter over Times Square. Suddenly, The Hunter was shot by an unknown assailant. Wolverine, Sabretooth, and Lady Deathstrike converged on the cage as the helicopter attempted to flee. In the confusion, the cage broke and released the Hunter in Darkness. Sabretooth and Lady Deathstrike continued their attack on Wolverine. The Hunter remembered that Wolverine had freed it years ago, and defended him from the villains. The fight was interrupted by the assailant, revealing herself as Emmy Doolin. She sought revenge for her father's obsession with the creature. However, the Hunter in Darkness escaped into the sewers. The Hunter encountered Albert and Elsie-Dee in the Morlock Alley, and joined them on their stealth bomber. It led them to a Blackfoot burial ground in Canada. The Hunter and Albert dug into a burial mound, and found a skeleton with adamantium claws. Albert ran a facial reconstruction program on the skull. They discovered the skeleton belonged to Wolverine, however the remains were over 200-years-old. Spiral sent The Hunter in Darkness, Albert, and Elsie-Dee through a time vortex into the past to learn more.

hunter stein.name: Hunter Stein
hunter stein.origin: Hunter Stein is Chase Stein's uncle and Victor Stein's brother. Hunter runs Track Consolidated Construction and Containment, which designs facilities to contain superpowered people who are either criminals or unable to control their abilities. Hunter would frequently visit his brother and the two would argue. Chase suspected that Hunter wanted to be let in on the Pride's criminal activity, though there is some indication that Hunter may have actually been trying to stop Victor's abuse of Janet. Whatever the truth, there was a fight between the two brothers, and Hunter stormed out of Victor's house. Shortly after this fight, Hunter was injured and had to have his hip and parts of his legs replaced. Chase believes that he accidentally ran Hunter over with his van as Hunter was leaving the house, though it is unclear how reliable his memory is. After the defeat of the Pride, Hunter inherited the Malibu beach house that the Runaways are staying in. When the Runaways broke into the house, unaware that he owned it, he chose not to intervene, not wishing to drive away his nephew, but when the house was suddenly hit by a drone, he hurried over to make sure everyone was okay, managing to pass through the forest that had been summoned by Klara. He offered to take care of the Runaways, but they refused.

hurricane dark riders.name: Hurricane (Dark Riders)
hurricane dark riders.origin: Hurricane was recruited into the second incarnation of the Dark Riders by Genesis. Alongside his teammates, Hurricane ambushed Foxbat in Egypt, deeming the former Dark Rider unworthy to live. The Dark Riders later encountered Cable, Storm, and Domino in the Morlock tunnels as they chased down Caliban, also found unworthy. In the ensuing battle, Hurricane fought Storm, declaring that he hoped she would be judged so that they could meet on the battlefield. Storm managed to best Hurricane, and Hard-Drive teleported the defeated Dark Riders to safety. The heroes tracked the Dark Riders back to Egypt, where Tusk led them into a trap. Hurricane summoned a sandstorm which enabled the others to strike at Storm and her allies. However, Storm dissipated the sandstorm which left the Dark Riders vulnerable. Gauntlet, enraged at Hurricane's multiple failures to defeat Storm, pointed his gun at Hurricane's head. Cable telekinetically pulled the gun from Gauntlet's hand and ordered the Dark Riders to surrender. Hard-Drive once again pulled his teammates from battle, including Hurricane. As punishment for his failed attempts to kill Storm, Hurricane was restrained in a glass tube alongside Foxbat, Cable, and other mutants, and had some of his power siphoned by Genesis. Under unknown circumstances, Hurricane rejoined the Dark Riders and assisted them in freeing the mutant Cyber from prison. Cyber soon learned that the Dark Riders were deceiving him and that they planned to use him to restore Wolverine's adamantium. The Riders succeeded in stripping Cyber of his adamantium, killing him. However, Wolverine's body rejected the process, causing an explosion. Hurricane and his teammate Lifeforce were impaled with adamantium shrapnel, killing them both. ===Necrosha=== Hurricane, along with a few other Dark Riders, was one of many deceased mutants to have been resurrected by Selene and the Transmode virus. The Dark Riders later resurfaced, hunting down and killing mutant healers as they believed their powers to be a violation of the natural order. This led to a battle with Magneto and the X-Men, as Hurricane and his team had targeted Elixir. The Dark Riders were eventually defeated, and Magneto killed the group by detonating explosives on their island.

fields.history: Hurricane was recruited into the second incarnation of the Dark Riders by Genesis. Alongside his teammates, Hurricane ambushed Foxbat in Egypt, deeming the former Dark Rider unworthy to live. The Dark Riders later encountered Cable, Storm, and Domino in the Morlock tunnels as they chased down Caliban, also found unworthy. In the ensuing battle, Hurricane fought Storm, declaring that he hoped she would be judged so that they could meet on the battlefield. Storm managed to best Hurricane, and Hard-Drive teleported the defeated Dark Riders to safety. The heroes tracked the Dark Riders back to Egypt, where Tusk led them into a trap. Hurricane summoned a sandstorm which enabled the others to strike at Storm and her allies. However, Storm dissipated the sandstorm which left the Dark Riders vulnerable. Gauntlet, enraged at Hurricane's multiple failures to defeat Storm, pointed his gun at Hurricane's head. Cable telekinetically pulled the gun from Gauntlet's hand and ordered the Dark Riders to surrender. Hard-Drive once again pulled his teammates from battle, including Hurricane. As punishment for his failed attempts to kill Storm, Hurricane was restrained in a glass tube alongside Foxbat, Cable, and other mutants, and had some of his power siphoned by Genesis. hurt john.name: Hurt John
hurt john.origin: Hurt John was recruited by Zeitgeist to join his new group the X-Cellent. He was sent with the others to the residence of Micky Holloran in order to find Katie Sawyer who was Holloran's girlfriend. Not knowing where she was, John told him that his companion Uno would liquefy his skeleton if he did not arrange a meeting with her tomorrow. Hurt John and X-Cellent attacked once again by blowing a hole through Micky's wall. As they approached Katie, Dead Girl appeared and tried to motivate Katie to teleport Micky and herself out of there to seek medical attention. But her words went unheard as John used his ability to draw the pain out of Dead Girl with tactile touch. Making her relive the torture gave the group enough time to make off with Katie. Back at their Death Valley headquarters, John stood by as Zeitgeist tried to convince Katie to join them as they were in need of a teleporter who could reassemble the body of Venus Dee Milo. Refusing to aid them, Katie was tortured by Cluney until Dead Girl appeared to intervene. John said he will take care of Dead Girl like he did before, but he was knocked off balance by an explosion caused X-Statix who arrived to thwart their plans. John battled against The A until a full on assault by Uno's optic blast gave the X-Cellent the upper hand in the fight. Katie ended up getting free and used her teleportation to get X-Statix out of there before John and the others could finish them off for good.

hussar.name: Hussar
hussar.origin: Hussar was one of the eight Guards chosen to battle the X-Men for the fate of the Phoenix - which had adopted the shape of Human Jean Grey at that time. Hussar later was part of a conspiracy to overthrow Shi'ar Empire Princess-Majestrix Lilandra Neramani, working alongside Lord Samédàr, Deathbird, and the Brood. She continued to work with the Guard after Lilandra regained power, however; she protected her Majestrix from a Kree Starforce assassination attempt during the Kree-Shi'ar Operation Galactic Storm conflict, and after a Shi'ar victory helped fend off a further attempt on her life by Ronan the Accuser's Inhuman assassins. However, Hussar was later punished for past crimes, and was banished to Earth during Maximum Security. She was eventually reinstated in the Guard.

hutsu.name: Hutsu
hutsu.origin: Hutsu was a spy for Imperial Japan during World War II. By 1942, he and his fellow spies had set themselves up as a sleepwalking cult operating just outside of New York City. Targeting those troubled with sleep-walking, not only those involved in American defense. Hutsu developed a special perfume that allowed him to influence those who were sleeping to reveal their secrets or carry out his orders. One such victim was Captain Corbin of the United States Army. Corbin faced court martial when he was caught seemingly selling secrets to the enemy. With Corbin's usefulness having come to an end, Hutsu used his perfume to order the sleep-walking Corbin to walk off the ledge outside of his apartment. Corbin's actions were seen by the Angel who failed in preventing Corbin from jumping to his death. Hutsu lingered on the scene long enough for the Angel to notice him and become suspicious. Hutsu then returned to his hideout where he began working on American spy Dorothy Ray in order to learn her secrets. This process was interrupted by the Angel who had tracked Hutsu to his hideout. During the ensuing fight, the Angel was exposed to Hutsu's gas and put under the spy's control. Convincing the Angel that he was a Japanese spy as well, Hutsu ordered the hero to assassinate Colonel Gardner, the chief of military intelligence in New York City. As the Angel carried out his task, Hutsu followed behind to insure that his unwitting agent carried out his orders. The Angel's strange behavior was noticed by military personnel who doused the hero with water, snapping him out of their control. Overhearing that the Angel forgot the location of his hideout but knew that a cab driver drove Hutsu there, Hutsu raced against military officials to silence the cabby. Hutsu succeeded in beating his pursuers there and killed the cabby. In a high speed chase with the Angel and military officials, Hutsu doused their driver with gas, causing them to crash. Military officials eventually tracked Hutsu down by putting the Angel back in a sleep-like trance to lead them to the hideout. There, the Angel bested Hutsu in combat and turned him over to the military. His fate following the end of World War II remains unrecorded.

hybrid agent diana.name: Hybrid (Agent Diana)
hybrid agent diana.origin: Agent Diana was an agent of S.H.I.E.L.D. She was hurt in an accident after trying to steal some organism that could attach itself to other organisms and became a mutated form of the organism herself seeking revenge. She found that Thaddeus Ross was in the hospital. However, she could not get close to him. She possessed a nurse, then she waited until Ross's daughter Betty left the room. When Betty left Hybrid went into the room, left nurse's body, and possessed the general. As Ross, she went to Betty who saw her father waking up. She saw that his eyes were not right and started to fight him. She tried to call Bruce Banner but Hybrid possessed her. As Betty, she contacted Bruce and his cousin She-Hulk, saying that they needed to infiltrate an underwater S.H.I.E.L.D. facility to stop a new weapon that Gabriel Jones was testing. They commandeered a submarine and entered the facility. However, they were captured by Jones. Hybrid understood that it was time to change the body, and by kissing Grey Hulk possessed him. While being kicked out of the base, Gabriel revealed to She-Hulk the story of who Diana was and how did she became like that. Hybrid tried to take control of the base using it as a weapon. She demanded that Gabriel transfer the control of all of S.H.I.E.L.D.'s nuclear silos to it or else she will flood the coast of California with massive waves. Gabriel denied and sent S.H.I.E.L.D. Cruisers to intercept the sea base. Hybrid sunk the cruisers using the facility's weapon, but this caused the reactor to overload, entering meltdown. The situation enraged Hybrid and Hulk's natural healing ability, combined with his anger, forced Hybrid out turning him into Green Hulk. Hybrid tried to possess Betty again, but Hulk punched her into unconsciousness. She woke up later and possessed a shark, swimming away before the facility exploded.

hydro.name: Hydro
hydro.origin: The Brothers Four claim to have been created and taught their magical powers by the wizard posing as Merlin for the purposes of seeking out and destroying Modred the Mystic. Their numbers included the earth elemental Mud, the fire element known as Fire, the water element known as Hydro, and the air element Aero. They were placed in stasis within a chest that eventually ended up beneath British Parliament. The brothers were inadvertently freed by two thieves seeking to recover stolen Nazi loot hidden in Parliment during World War II. Materializing in a cavern below Stonehenge and began capturing tourists to drain them of the energies they needed to pull Modred back in time and return him to their master. Their arrival drew the visiting heroes Spider-Woman, the Fantastic Four's Thing and the Thing's girlfriend Alicia Masters. The Thing and Spider-Woman battled the creatures until Modred -- sensing the elemental's arrival came. Modred then used his superior magics to turn each elemental against their opposite, the powers of one cancelling out the other, destroying the Four Brothers before they could complete their mission.

hydron elementals.name: Hydron (Elementals)
hydron elementals.origin: Hydron was a member of the Elementals and commanded the power of water. He was also the most bloodthirsty of the group. The Elementals were supposedly cast out of their own universe millennia ago. They arrived on Earth even before Atlantis was built, and established a kingdom. They were undefeated, until they tried to extend its reaches into the land that would later be known as Egypt. Here, a young warrior named Dann and a wizard named Garret joined their two souls to arcane magics and created the Ruby Scarab. In the hands of Dann, this magical item sapped the powers of the Elementals and banished them to another universe. Nothing more was heard of the Elementals until the modern age when they transported the Living Mummy from New York City in order to enlist him in their search for the Ruby Scarab, which they sought to help them take control of the world. After the Elementals took the city of Cairo hostage under a force field, Zephyr revealed herself to be opposed to the others, helping N'Kantu, Doctor Skarab and the others to defeat her former brethren. These three Elementals were then banished from Earth by Alexi Skarab using the power of the Ruby Scarab. Hydron alongside the other Elementals later returned to Earth in search of Zephyr and the Scarab. They fought Ms. Marvel and their former ally Hecate, they were defeated one by one.

hyinar.name: Hyinar
hyinar.species: Snark enhanced by use of Inhuman powers
hyinar.origin: The third prince of the Zn'rx Royal Blood, Hyinar initiated Snarkwar (later known as the Hyinar Usurpation), a civil war for succession in his homeworld. In order to provide his faction with an advantage, Prince Hyinar and his crew set out to find "weaponworlds," planets inhabited by super-powered beings from whom they could steal their abilities, or "weapons" as he called them. To this end, the beings abducted by Prince Hyinar and his men were placed in crystal tubes that acted as power transfers. After granting one of his men, Dyngo, the ability to render himself gaseous and release energy bolts from Kymellian sorcerers, Prince Hyinar targeted a crew of Inhumans that landed on Centauri-IV. The first Inhuman they attacked was Gorgon, from whom Hyinar stole his hooves. The Snarks then abducted a group of Inhumans and Universal Inhumans from the Circle of Testing Fire, and distributed their powers among themselves. Hyinar obtained the powers of Crystal and Flint. thumb|left Prince Hyinar, Dyngo and Koyoti proceeded to attack the remaining Inhuman visitors as well as the Universal Inhuman Court, who were investigating a Skyspear in the Great Desert. Hyinar's plan was interrupted by the intervention of the depowered Inhumans, who managed to escape custody. Flint entered in contact with the Skyspear to regain his powers, and formed a spiked cube out of earth with which he crushed Hyinar and Dyngo to death. Though Hyinar died, the Hyinar Usurpation derailed the attempts at modernizing the succession process, and led to the rise to power and (brief) rule of Stote.

hylas.name: Hylas
hylas.origin: Hylas was the son of Theiodamas, king of the Dryopians. When Hercules killed his father, he spared the boy due to his great beauty which bewitched all who looked upon him, and made him his companion and arms-bearer. In 1289 BCE he accompanied Herc and the Argonauts during the Quest for the Golden Fleece, sailing off the coast of Mysia where he was abducted by water nymphs and lost to Hercules forever. Hercules refused to stop searching for him, and so was left behind by the Argonauts. Only after Hercules' death and apotheosis would he learn what really happened to Hylas. Then and there, though, it was if the Earth had simply swallowed him up.

hyllus.name: Hyllus
hyllus.species: Hyllus is a mortal man descended from the House of Perseus, circa 13th BC. Part-Olympian Hybrid
hyllus.origin: ===Early Life=== Hyllus was the son of Hercules and Deianira. Hyllus married Iole. He was a great warrior like his father. Alongside the armies of Thebes and Athens, Hyllus joined his half-brothers and their supporters in ousting King Eurystheus from the throne of Mycenae and excising a form of vengeance over much of the Peloponnesus for lands promised to their father. He dragged him to Alcmena, Hercules' mother. He tried to explain to her he was doing Hera's will, but Alcmena pierced his eyes and Hyllus beheaded him.

hypernova.name: Hypernova
hypernova.origin: Hypernova was a failed subguardian recruit of the Hussar class, believed to have failed due to her inability to control the lethality of her powers. She joined the Death Commandos as a result since there were no restrictions on what she could do. On their first assignment, she and the other Death Commandos went to Earth where they were tasked with wiping out the Grey Genome. They managed to wipe out almost all the relatives of Jean Grey but failed to kill Rachel Summers before being defeated. Following this, the Shi'ar Empire broke out into a civil war and the Death Commandos remained loyal to Araki. The Death Commandos were next tasked by Oracle with killing Deathbird and anyone with her. They boarded Deathbird's escort shuttle and along with Flaw and Offset ran into Magik. She asked them if they were human, and when they said no, she let go of her powers and killed all of them. Meanwhile, Black Cloak watched as all their pulses flatlined.

hypno creature.name: Hypno-Creature
hypno creature.origin: The Hypno-Creature was used by the natives of a two-dimensional world to pursue and detain intruders. Although normally very small, when exposed to certain fumes, it would grow to enormous size. When a human teenager entered the two-dimensional world and discovered that its people were plotting to invade Earth, they unleashed the Hypno-Creature against him. However, he was able to reflect the creature's eye beams back upon it with a shard of crystal, turning it against its masters.

weaknesses: The creature was vulnerable to its own hypnotic vision.
